es.summary: Antibiótico glicopéptido usado por vía intravenosa para infecciones graves de gram‑positivos; la infusión rápida puede producir síndrome del hombre rojo.
key_points: El síndrome del hombre rojo ocurre con infusión >10 mg/kg/h.
Presenta enrojecimiento facial, prurito y hipotensión.
Premedicación con antihistamínico reduce la reacción.
Monitorear signos vitales durante la primera hora.
Detener la infusión y notificar al médico si la reacción es severa.

mechanism: Se une al extremo D‑Ala‑D‑Ala de la pared celular bacteriana inhibiendo la síntesis de peptidoglicano.
Libera histamina de mastocitos cuando se administra rápidamente, provocando enrojecimiento y prurito.
indications: Infecciones graves por Staphylococcus aureus resistente a meticilina (MRSA).
Endocarditis bacteriana, sepsis y meningitis por cocos gram‑positivos.
contraindications: Insuficiencia renal grave sin ajuste de dosis.
Uso concomitante con anestésicos que aumentan ototoxicidad (ej. fenciclidina).
adverse_effects: Enrojecimiento facial y prurito (síndrome del hombre rojo).
nursing_care: Verificar alergias y función renal (creatinina, depuración).
Infundir a no más de 10 mg/kg/h (mínimo 60 min).
Monitorear presión arterial, frecuencia cardíaca y temperatura cada 15 min la primera hora.
Tener antihistamínico (diphenhydramine) listo antes de iniciar la infusión.
Detener la infusión y notificar al médico si aparecen enrojecimiento intenso, hipotensión o dificultad respiratoria.
patient_teaching: Informar que puede presentar enrojecimiento y picazón; reportar cualquier molestia.
Explicar la importancia de la infusión lenta y del premedicamento si se indica.
Mantener hidratación adecuada y avisar si nota cambios auditivos.
No interrumpir la infusión sin avisar al personal de salud.

outcomes: Sin signos de reacción alérgica durante y después de la infusión.
Presión arterial mantenida dentro de 90‑140/60‑90 mmHg durante la terapia.

interventions.action: Verificar historial de alergias y función renal antes de iniciar la infusión.
interventions.rationale: Identifica pacientes con mayor riesgo de reacción y permite ajuste de dosis.

interventions.action: Administrar antihistamínico (ej. difenhidramina) 30 min antes de la vancomicina si está indicado.
interventions.rationale: Previene la liberación de histamina y reduce la incidencia del síndrome del hombre rojo.

interventions.action: Controlar signos vitales cada 15 min durante la primera hora de infusión.
interventions.rationale: Detecta tempranamente hipotensión o taquicardia asociada a reacción.

interventions.action: Detener la infusión y notificar al médico si aparecen enrojecimiento intenso, prurito, hipotensión o dificultad respiratoria.
interventions.rationale: Interrumpe la exposición al agente desencadenante y permite intervención médica inmediata.

interventions.action: Documentar cualquier signo de reacción y las acciones tomadas.
interventions.rationale: Facilita la continuidad del cuidado y la evaluación de la efectividad de las medidas preventivas.

en.summary: Glycopeptide antibiotic administered intravenously for severe gram‑positive infections; rapid infusion can cause red man syndrome.
key_points: Red man syndrome occurs with infusion >10 mg/kg/h.
Presents with facial flushing, pruritus and hypotension.
Premedication with antihistamine reduces the reaction.
Monitor vital signs during the first hour.
Stop the infusion and notify the physician if the reaction is severe.

mechanism: Binds the D‑Ala‑D‑Ala terminus of bacterial cell wall peptidoglycan, inhibiting synthesis.
Releases histamine from mast cells when administered rapidly, causing flushing and pruritus.
indications: Severe infections with methicillin‑resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA).
Bacterial endocarditis, sepsis and meningitis caused by gram‑positive cocci.
contraindications: Severe renal insufficiency without dose adjustment.
Concurrent use with anesthetics that increase ototoxicity (e.g., phencyclidine).
adverse_effects: Facial flushing and pruritus (red man syndrome).
nursing_care: Check allergies and renal function (creatinine, clearance).
Infuse no more than 10 mg/kg/h (minimum 60 min).
Monitor blood pressure, heart rate and temperature every 15 min during the first hour.
Have antihistamine (diphenhydramine) ready before starting the infusion.
Stop the infusion and notify the physician if intense flushing, hypotension or respiratory difficulty occurs.
patient_teaching: Inform that flushing and itching may occur; report any discomfort.
Explain the importance of slow infusion and premedication if indicated.
Maintain adequate hydration and report any hearing changes.
Do not interrupt the infusion without notifying health staff.

outcomes: No signs of allergic reaction during and after infusion.
Blood pressure maintained within 90‑140/60‑90 mmHg during therapy.

interventions.action: Verify allergy history and renal function before starting the infusion.
interventions.rationale: Identifies patients at higher risk of reaction and allows dose adjustment.

interventions.action: Administer antihistamine (e.g., diphenhydramine) 30 min before vancomycin if indicated.
interventions.rationale: Prevents histamine release and reduces incidence of red man syndrome.

interventions.action: Check vital signs every 15 min during the first hour of infusion.
interventions.rationale: Detects early hypotension or tachycardia associated with reaction.

interventions.action: Stop the infusion and notify the physician if intense flushing, pruritus, hypotension or respiratory difficulty occurs.
interventions.rationale: Interrupts exposure to the trigger and allows immediate medical intervention.

interventions.action: Document any signs of reaction and actions taken.
interventions.rationale: Facilitates continuity of care and evaluation of preventive measures effectiveness.

key_points.3.quote: As such, it is critical that the nurse remain with the patient for at least the first fifteen minutes of the transfusion (or longer if required by the agency’s policy) and monitor vital signs.

key_points.4.quote: In the event of moderate reactions, stop the transfusion, and notify the provider.

sections.adverse_effects.3.quote: Some drugs are administered more slowly, however, such as pushing 40 mg IV furosemide IV over two minutes to prevent hearing loss.

sections.adverse_effects.4.quote: Common symptoms of an allergic reaction include flushing, hives, rash, pruritus , difficulty breathing, laryngeal edema , wheezing, and possible anaphylaxis .

sections.nursing_care.4.quote: If you suspect a reaction, immediately stop the transfusion, and notify the provider.

sections.patient_teaching.0.quote: The nurse must also explain the procedure to the patient and inform the patient to immediately report symptoms of a possible blood transfusion reaction, such as sweating, chills, chest pain, shortness of breath, headache, back pain, nausea, vomiting, or itching.
